Some AI tools stop when you stop typing.
Others keep working while you sleep.
Here's how to tell them apart.
A chat assistant, like Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, answers when you ask, and then it stops.
It's best for thinking, drafting and research.
A desktop agent, like Claude Cowork, Codex or Cursor, works on your computer or your files.
It builds spreadsheets, sites and code while you watch, or while you step away for a while.
An always-on agent runs on its own cloud computer.
It checks your apps on a schedule and comes to you first.
Grok Bot can log in to your web apps with its own browser.
A dot in ChatGPT follows custom rules about what it may do alone.
Claude Duet sends a morning brief and asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything.
Parts of all three are still preview or beta, so build on the pattern, not on any one menu.
